events.headline: Bears' Kyle Monangai hyperextends knee in practice, out multiple weeks
events.detail: Monangai, projected as Chicago's RB2 behind D'Andre Swift, hyperextended his right knee Sunday (Aug. 16) after being tackled from behind during a non-padded 11-on-11 period — his second camp injury after an earlier soft-tissue issue. ESPN's Jeremy Fowler reports the MRI outcome is considered positive (no structural damage), but he's still projected to miss multiple weeks, with about four weeks left before Chicago's Week 1 opener.
events.so_what: This format's 5-man bench rewards a clean handcuff assignment — Roschon Johnson is the practical beneficiary of Monangai's lost camp reps for the RB3 job behind Swift, while Monangai himself slides from a speculative complementary-back price to a wait-and-see grade until he's back running. Swift's bell-cow workload projection is unaffected either way, so this is a depth-chart note rather than a top-of-roster shift ahead of this league's 2026-08-23 draft.

events.headline: Giants host free agent Najee Harris amid crowded, injury-thinned RB room
events.detail: New York hosted veteran Najee Harris (four straight 1,000-yard seasons in Pittsburgh before tearing his Achilles three games into a 2025 stint with the Chargers) for a visit Monday (Aug. 17). The Giants' backfield already features the Skattebo/Tracy co-starter split from the Aug. 11 depth chart plus Devin Singletary, and depth back Dante Miller was hurt in the preseason opener against Minnesota. Harris previously worked with Giants senior offensive assistant Greg Roman in Pittsburgh; no signing confirmed yet.
events.so_what: Updates the Aug. 11 item — a team already fielding a genuine committee going shopping for a veteran free agent is a bearish signal for both Skattebo's and Tracy's paths to a clean workhorse price in this format's volume-friendly scoring, since a Harris addition (even on a prove-it deal, and himself coming off a major injury) would only muddy the touch split further. Don't lock either incumbent into a set draft-round price until the roster math resolves, ideally before this league's 2026-08-23 draft.

events.headline: McCaffrey still hasn't practiced since Aug. 8; hold-in speculation now surfacing
events.detail: McCaffrey first sat out Monday (Aug. 10) — actually dating to Aug. 8 per updated reporting — with what the team called tightness and remained out of practice through Aug. 18, more than a week and a half missed. Shanahan continues to voice confidence he'll be ready for the Sept. 10 opener in Australia, but league observers are now floating hold-in speculation tied to McCaffrey's non-guaranteed $12.5M 2026 salary, on top of the earlier read that this echoes his 2024 camp absence that turned into a Week 1 inactive.
events.so_what: Updates the Aug. 15/16 items — still this format's clearest bell-cow RB1 on talent and touches, but a contract-dispute angle is a materially different risk than simple maintenance rest, since a real hold-in could bleed into September reps and timing with Purdy. Not a fade at current price, but recheck for an actual practice-return date or a contract-restructure report before locking in a clean RB1 grade ahead of this league's 2026-08-23 draft.

events.headline: Jets' Breece Hall exits practice with strained groin, imaging planned
events.detail: Hall left Monday's (Aug. 17) practice early with a groin strain after going down untouched following a catch. Coach Aaron Glenn told reporters 'I don't think it was a big deal, but I want to make sure I get the evaluation on that,' and Hall will undergo imaging to confirm severity. He had played in New York's preseason opener against Tampa Bay (4 carries, 16 yards) before this.
events.so_what: Hall is a clean bell-cow price in this format's volume-friendly scoring off a 1,065-yard, 36-catch 2025; a same-day 'not a big deal' framing from the coach keeps this a watch item rather than a markdown, but any lingering absence a week before this league's 2026-08-23 draft would open early-down work behind him. Recheck for the imaging result before locking in a clean RB1/2 grade.

events.headline: Cardinals' Jeremiyah Love suffers high ankle sprain, unlikely to play again in preseason
events.detail: Love, the No. 3 overall pick who'd just been confirmed (Aug. 13 item) as the Cardinals' preseason snap-share leader over Tyler Allgeier, sustained a high ankle sprain against the Raiders on Thursday (Aug. 13/14) after being brought down awkwardly on a catch near the goal line. Coach Mike LaFleur told reporters Love would miss at least the next week; follow-up reporting through Aug. 17 has him unlikely to play again this preseason, with the team hopeful for a Week 1 return (Sept. 13 at the Chargers) roughly four weeks out.
events.so_what: Updates and reverses the Aug. 13 item's bullish framing — a high ankle sprain is a real markdown on what had just become a clean low-end-RB1 price, since this format's bell-cow premium needs him on the field, not on a four-week runway that barely clears Week 1. Allgeier (and James Conner once fully cleared) are the near-term beneficiaries; don't lock Love in at his pre-injury price for this league's 2026-08-23 draft without a real practice-return checkpoint first.

events.headline: Panthers' Jonathon Brooks gets real preseason run in first live action since 2024 ACL tear
events.detail: With Hubbard held out (hamstring, Aug. 13 item), Brooks started and played 4 of the Panthers' 9 first-team offensive snaps in Saturday's (Aug. 15) preseason opener at Buffalo — 3 carries for 5 yards and 1 catch for 9 yards — his first game action since Week 14 of his rookie 2024 season. Panthers.com reports the staff intends to keep featuring him as a pass-catcher through the preseason.
events.so_what: Updates the Aug. 13 item — actual first-team preseason snaps (not just practice buzz) is a stronger signal of a real complementary role forming behind Hubbard, and the pass-catching usage plan makes Brooks more than a pure handcuff in this format's 2-FLEX math if Hubbard's hamstring lingers. Hubbard remains the safer lead-back price for now given no firm setback reported, but Brooks is worth a FLEX-speculative price ahead of this league's 2026-08-23 draft.

events.headline: Kittle 'ahead of schedule' on Achilles rehab, targeting Week 1 opener in Australia
events.detail: Kittle, on PUP since camp opened after tearing his Achilles in San Francisco's Jan. 11 playoff win, told reporters Saturday (Aug. 15) 'we've attacked this the right way, and we're very much ahead of schedule, and hopefully I'm on the field here in a little bit,' adding his surgeon's message was 'push it, just don't be an idiot.' He remains on PUP (not yet practicing) but is targeting the Week 1 opener against the Rams in Melbourne, Australia (Sept. 10-ish window). GM John Lynch said in late July the team is 'thrilled with his progress' but will be careful given the international-game timing.
events.so_what: This format's punt-TE doctrine (league-profile.md §4) treats a clean Kittle Week 1 as a real elite-TE outcome, not a lock — he's still not practicing as of Aug 15, and the Australia-opener timing gives the staff real incentive to hold him out an extra week or two even if healthy. Don't price him as a locked Week 1 starter yet; recheck once he's actually off PUP and taking padded reps, ideally before this league's 2026-08-23 draft.

events.headline: RJ Harvey gets first-team touches but modest numbers in Broncos preseason debut
events.detail: Harvey took all the first-team carries and ran more routes than third-down back J.K. Dobbins in Denver's preseason opener (Aug. 15), but the return was thin: 7 carries for 25 yards (two runs of 18 combined, the other five going for six total) and 1 catch for 4 yards on 2 targets. Sean Payton said afterward Harvey could have been more patient on one run and that the staff will get him more work between the tackles, calling him 'an extremely instinctive runner.'
events.so_what: The touch distribution (all 1s-work over Dobbins, who remains limited with a soft-tissue issue per the Aug. 14 item) is the clean signal for a locked-in early-down role in this format's bell-cow-friendly scoring, even though the per-carry numbers themselves don't move the needle — hold Harvey at his current early-round RB price and treat this as role confirmation, not a production data point, ahead of this league's 2026-08-23 draft.

events.headline: Bills' DJ Moore grabs ankle after big preseason debut catch, avoids serious injury
events.detail: Moore opened his Bills preseason debut Saturday (Aug. 15) against Carolina by hauling in three catches for 61 yards on Buffalo's first two drives, including a 33-yard connection with Josh Allen, before grabbing his right ankle/foot on the sideline after his last catch and walking off under his own power. He gave Allen a thumbs-up on the way out, and early reporting indicates the injury is not considered serious, though it ended his day with most of the starting offense already out of the game.
events.so_what: The on-field connection with Allen is the clean signal this format cares about for a locked-in WR1 price in Buffalo's offense; the ankle scare reads as precautionary given he walked off and gave a thumbs-up, but confirm he's back to full practice before this league's 2026-08-23 draft since any lingering ankle issue would cut into a route-running-dependent receiver's value.

events.headline: Jaguars' first depth chart lists Bhayshul Tuten and Chris Rodriguez Jr. as RB co-starters
events.detail: Jacksonville's first unofficial depth chart of camp lists 2025 fifth-round pick Tuten and Rodriguez separated only by an "OR" atop the running back room, with veteran Ameer Abdullah also in the mix for touches. All three are expected to see work in Friday's preseason slate as the staff sorts out the pecking order.
events.so_what: Another true committee is this format's worst RB outcome since 2 FLEX and half-PPR reward one back consolidating touches, not a three-way split — this caps both Tuten and Rodriguez at speculative RB4/handcuff prices rather than a clean starter valuation until preseason snap counts show real separation. Watch the next couple of preseason games before locking either into a draft-day price.

events.headline: Nabers not suited up for Giants' preseason opener, still not contact-cleared
events.detail: Nabers was not in uniform for Saturday's (Aug. 15) preseason opener against Minnesota, one game removed from the Aug. 13 milestone of catching passes on his first four non-contact team reps. He still has not been cleared for contact, making it a real question whether he manages even a cameo before Week 1. JuJu Smith-Schuster (knee) and Jalin Hyatt (ankle) also sat out, giving young receivers Malachi Fields and Dalen Cambre an extended look.
events.so_what: Updates the Aug. 13 item — non-contact team reps were real progress, but sitting the actual preseason opener with no contact clearance yet is a sober reset on how close he is to Week 1, not a setback exactly, just a reminder the runway is short. Hold at a modest discount to a clean WR1 price and watch for an actual contact-practice clearance as the next real trigger before this league's 2026-08-23 draft. Direct stash relevance for bwalsh89, this league's Nabers/Dart owner from 2025.

events.headline: Nacua left off NFL's Friday suspension round, but case stays open with legal process ongoing
events.detail: Nacua left Tuesday's (Aug. 11) joint practice against Dallas with a groin injury the Rams call minor, and his practice reps remained limited through midweek. On his separate personal-conduct-policy case (a civil lawsuit alleges he bit a woman and made an antisemitic remark at a New Year's Eve party; no criminal charges filed), the NFL announced a round of suspensions Friday (Aug. 14) covering other players (James Pearce 8 games, plus Phidarian Mathis, Nazeeh Johnson, Dorance Armstrong) but did not include Nacua. Per a same-day report, his case differs because the underlying civil litigation is still active — his attorneys recently got a key witness deposition pushed past Sept. 7 — and the NFL typically lets that process play out before ruling, meaning a decision could land after Week 1 rather than before it.
events.so_what: Updates the prior version of this item — being passed over in Friday's suspension batch lowers the odds of a Week 1 absence specifically, which is the near-term number this format's draft-day math cares about, but it does not close the risk out: a mid-season suspension is still very much alive given the open litigation. Treat Nacua as safer for Week 1 than the Aug 11-14 framing suggested, but keep a small in-season discount versus a totally clean top-5 WR price, and recheck for a ruling right up to this league's 2026-08-23 draft.

events.headline: Burden doing light on-field work, sprinting routes, as groin injury trends toward a Week 1 return
events.detail: Burden's Saturday (Aug. 8) groin injury will keep him out through Chicago's preseason slate, but he was seen doing light work Saturday (Aug. 15), including sprints from the 40 to the end zone, per Adam Schefter — the first real on-field progress reported since the injury. Coach Ben Johnson still expects him back for the Sept. 13 regular-season opener at Carolina. Burden is stepping into the WR2 role opposite Rome Odunze now that Chicago traded DJ Moore to Buffalo, with Johnson comparing his ceiling to Amon-Ra St. Brown's.
events.so_what: Updates the Aug. 10 item — sprinting work a week after the injury is the clearest positive signal yet for a clean Week 1 return, keeping Burden's expanding target share (Moore fully gone from the room) priced as a breakout-candidate WR2/3 in this format's half-PPR/normal-depth WR math. Recheck once he's back to full team drills or a preseason snap count.

events.headline: Saints rookie WR Jordyn Tyson suffers hamstring injury in joint practice, could linger to Week 1
events.detail: Tyson, the No. 8 overall pick who fell out of top-5 consideration partly due to hamstring issues at Arizona State, injured his right hamstring Thursday (Aug. 13) in joint practice against Jacksonville after his foot slipped and he was pushed from behind following a catch. Coach Kellen Moore declined to give a timeline Thursday (Aug. 14): 'I don't have a doctor in front of my name, so I'm not going to jump to put together a timeline on it,' but said it could extend into Week 1. He was already slated to sit out that Saturday's preseason game.
events.so_what: A first-round rookie WR with a recurring hamstring history losing camp reps right before this league's 2026-08-23 draft is a real discount on his rookie-WR price in this format's normal-depth WR math — treat him as a wait-and-see Week 1 role bet rather than a locked-in target earner, and watch for the actual return-to-practice date as the next checkpoint.

events.headline: MarShawn Lloyd starts and takes every first-drive snap in Packers' preseason opener as Jacobs sits with groin injury and live suspension risk
events.detail: With Jacobs out (groin, first reported Aug. 6), Lloyd started Green Bay's preseason opener Thursday (Aug. 13) and took every snap on the first drive, working on early downs, in the passing game and in pass protection. Separately, ESPN's Adam Schefter reported this week (Aug. 11-14) that Jacobs' personal-conduct-policy investigation (stemming from a May 2026 domestic-disturbance call with no charges filed) remains open with the league still weighing discipline, and a suspension is a real possibility before Week 1; the policy sets a six-game floor for a first domestic-violence violation. Head coach Matt LaFleur said Friday (Aug. 14) that Jacobs could return to practice as soon as next week, likely coming back late in the week if he does, and continues to call the groin injury not serious.
events.so_what: Updates the Aug. 11/13 items — LaFleur's 'back next week' framing caps the groin issue itself as a short-term markdown, but the genuinely live suspension threat with no resolution timeline is still the bigger risk to Jacobs' draft price: a multi-week absence to open the season would hand Lloyd real starting-caliber volume in this format's bell-cow-friendly scoring. Worth actually rostering Lloyd as insurance given the shallow 5-man bench, and shading Jacobs down from a clean early-round RB price until the league rules, ideally before this league's 2026-08-23 draft.

events.headline: Dobbins limited to individual work as Broncos beat Falcons 27-7 in preseason opener; Coleman gets extensive run
events.detail: Dobbins remained limited to individual drills for Friday's (Aug. 14) preseason opener at Atlanta and did not play, still working back from the soft-tissue issue first reported Aug. 10. With Dobbins out, rookie Jonah Coleman got an extensive workload in the 27-7 win, continuing the camp buzz around his role.
events.so_what: Updates the Aug. 10 item — a full missed preseason game, not just a practice absence, is a real accumulation of lost reps for Dobbins against a rookie who keeps taking advantage of every opportunity handed to him. Still hold Dobbins as the lean for Denver's early-down role, but Coleman's price now needs to reflect genuine handcuff-plus-touchdown-usurper upside rather than a pure camp-buzz speculative flier; recheck once Dobbins is back to full team drills.

events.headline: 49ers' Ricky Pearsall undergoes season-ending PCL surgery
events.detail: Pearsall announced on Instagram Thursday (Aug. 13) that he had surgery to repair the PCL in his right knee, ending his 2026 season before it started. The knee had been persistently swollen through camp after he first injured it in Week 4 of 2025; his targeted recovery window is roughly nine months, putting a return around mid-May 2027 OTAs. He's played just 20 of a possible 51 regular-season games across his first three NFL seasons.
events.so_what: San Francisco's WR2 job behind Mike Evans (Aug. 11 item) is now fully vacant before the draft, not just contested — Deebo Samuel is the likeliest full-time beneficiary of the vacated snaps in Kyle Shanahan's run-funnel offense, with Jauan Jennings the clear No. 3. In half-PPR/2-FLEX, this removes a name some boards still carried as a discount buy and nudges Samuel's price up a notch in the McCaffrey/Kittle/Evans-led target pecking order.

events.headline: Titans' Pollard-Spears split looks genuinely even in preseason opener under new OC Brian Daboll
events.detail: In Thursday's (Aug. 13) preseason opener, Pollard played 57% of snaps (50% of designed rushes, 33% route participation, 2 catches for 11 yards, 35 rush yards) against Spears' 43% of snaps (38% of rush attempts, 50% route participation, a rushing TD on 3 carries for 2 yards). The beat read: "the coaching staff has told us multiple times that they view Pollard and Spears interchangeably, which matches Week 1 of the preseason." Daboll was hired as Tennessee's OC this offseason under new HC Robert Saleh.
events.so_what: This format's top RB tier wants one back consolidating touches, not a genuine timeshare — an actual even preseason split under a new play-caller is a real markdown on Pollard's price relative to a clean lead-back valuation, and it bumps Spears from pure handcuff to a real FLEX-relevant piece if the split holds. Both currently project more as touchdown-or-bust RB3s than clean starters; recheck preseason Week 2 usage.

events.headline: Browns name Deshaun Watson starter for preseason opener; Shedeur Sanders gets the start Aug. 22
events.detail: Coach Todd Monken confirmed this week that Watson starts Cleveland's preseason opener Saturday (Aug. 15) at Chicago, with Sanders set to start preseason Week 2 against Buffalo on Aug. 22. Monken said both will play meaningful snaps in the opener, including a two-minute drill each, and the preseason finale vs. New England (Aug. 27) will factor into the Week 1 decision.
events.so_what: Updates the Aug. 8 item — a structured, alternating-starts plan (not a clear front-runner emerging) confirms Cleveland's QB1 job is still genuinely open into September. This format pays no draft capital for either passer, but the battle stays the key swing factor for Njoku and the Browns' receiving corps' target stability, and it's relevant for mfkr and DiaperDutyDaddy (this league's rounds 2-4 QB-sniping threats) tracking a possible in-season Sanders takeover.

events.headline: DeVonta Smith misses seventh straight practice, but pre-practice route work signals a return is close
events.detail: Smith sat out Thursday's (Aug. 13) practice for a seventh consecutive session with the hamstring injury first reported Aug. 4, but worked through route-running drills with trainers beforehand — a step ahead of rookie Makai Lemon, who remains in a similar limbo. The Eagles open the preseason Saturday (Aug. 15) against Baltimore.
events.so_what: Updates the Aug. 11 item — seven missed practices is a real stretch, but the pre-practice route work is the clearest 'getting close' signal yet, and beat coverage now floats a return as soon as next week. Half-PPR target-hog scoring keeps Smith a locked-in WR1 price on the 'not serious' framing that's held throughout; recheck once he's actually back in team drills.

events.headline: Vikings' first unofficial depth chart lists Aaron Jones and Jordan Mason as RB co-starters
events.detail: Minnesota's first depth chart of the preseason, released Wednesday (Aug. 12), lists Jones and Mason separated only by an "OR" at the top of the running back room. Mason started all five games Jones missed in 2025 and finished with 758 yards and 6 TDs on 159 carries to Jones' 548 yards and 2 TDs; Jones remains the clearly superior receiving option. Zavier Scott, Demond Claiborne and Jermar Jefferson round out the room.
events.so_what: A true committee is this format's worst RB outcome since 2 FLEX and half-PPR reward one back consolidating touches, not a timeshare — an "OR" atop the unofficial chart is a real markdown on Jones' price relative to a clean lead-back valuation, though Jones' receiving-game edge keeps him the safer bet in Kevin O'Connell's scheme. Watch joint-practice and preseason snap splits before locking either into a set draft-round price.

events.headline: Croskey-Merritt stays 'firmly entrenched' as Commanders RB1 despite Rachaad White's strong joint-practice showing
events.detail: In Wednesday's (Aug. 12) joint practice with Miami, White broke a long outside-zone run showing good contact balance and continued building on the pass-catching role he's carved out this camp, but beat reporters still have Croskey-Merritt as the clear starter given his fit in Washington's new outside-zone scheme. Jeremy McNichols and rookie Kaytron Allen round out the room.
events.so_what: Half-PPR volume scoring rewards Croskey-Merritt's early-down role, but White's receiving-game separation keeps him relevant in a format where 2 FLEX can start a legitimate passing-down back — price Croskey-Merritt as the lead-back RB2/3 and White as a flex-worthy handcuff/PPR complement, not purely speculative, especially with Laremy Tunsil's blindside injury (Aug. 9 item) adding pressure to protect Jayden Daniels' checkdown game.

events.headline: Holani tops Seahawks' preseason RB depth chart over rookie Price with Charbonnet still on PUP
events.detail: Seattle's preseason depth chart (Aug. 12) lists Holani as the starting running back with first-round rookie Jadarian Price backing him up, while Charbonnet remains sidelined on the PUP list recovering from the ACL tear that ended his 2025 season, with ESPN reporting he may not return until late in 2026. Holani and Price have alternated first-team reps through camp, with free-agent addition Emanuel Wilson working mostly with the second unit. New OC Brian Fleury (replacing Klint Kubiak) is calling the offense.
events.so_what: Another crowded backfield is this format's worst RB outcome — 2 FLEX and half-PPR reward one back consolidating touches, and Seattle now has three-plus bodies (Holani, Price, Wilson, and eventually Charbonnet) mixing in with no clear hierarchy. Holani's depth-chart nod plus early receiving-down usage makes him the safer near-term price, Price the higher-variance rookie speculative add; neither should be priced as a clean starter until preseason snap counts show real separation, and Charbonnet's return timeline (real question mark past Week 1) caps the whole room's value ahead of this league's 2026-08-23 draft.

events.headline: Giants list Cam Skattebo and Tyrone Tracy Jr. as co-starters on first unofficial depth chart
events.detail: New York's first depth chart of camp, released ahead of the preseason opener against Minnesota, lists Skattebo and Tracy as co-starters at running back — the only offensive position without a clear No. 1. Tracy opened 2025 as the starter but was passed on the depth chart even after returning from injury, with Skattebo nearly doubling his snap count in Weeks 4-5 before his own rookie-season-ending ankle injury; Devin Singletary rounds out the room's top three.
events.so_what: A true committee is this format's worst RB outcome — 2 FLEX and half-PPR reward one back who consolidates touches, not a 1a/1b split, so neither Skattebo nor Tracy should be priced as a clean RB2 off this alone. Track joint-practice and preseason-game snap counts as the real signal; whichever back separates first is the one worth the earlier pick.

events.headline: 49ers' Mike Evans missed a week of camp with quad strain, back in pads but not yet full
events.detail: Evans, San Francisco's presumptive WR1 after signing this offseason, missed about a week of practice with a quad strain before returning in pads to Tuesday's (Aug. 11) joint practice against Tennessee, though he did not participate in the joint drills themselves and sat out that Thursday's preseason opener in street clothes. Coach Kyle Shanahan called it minor: 'He's got a little quad right now... we're being smart with him, but he's going to be good to go,' targeting the Sept. 10 Week 1 opener at the Rams.
events.so_what: Directly informs the Aug. 13 Pearsall item's target-share math — Evans is still the presumed top target in Kyle Shanahan's offense ahead of Deebo Samuel and Jauan Jennings, but a lost week of camp reps with Brock Purdy at his age (33 in Aug.) is a real chemistry-and-durability flag for a clean WR1 price. Watch for him back to full, unlimited practice reps as the next signal before this league's 2026-08-23 draft.
